reports.title: Griffon Corporation Announces Annual and Fourth Quarter Results

guidance.heading: 2027 Outlook
section: Griffon expects fiscal 2027 revenue and adjusted EBITDA to be consistent with the prior year at $1.85 billion and $460 million, respectively. Free cash flow, including capital expenditures of $60.0 million, is expected to approximate income from continuing operations, with depreciation of $26.0 million and amortization of $15.0 million. Fiscal year 2027 interest expense is expected to be $50.0 million, inclusive of interest income from notes receivable. Griffon’s normalized tax rate is expected to be 28%.

desk.headline: Revenue up 3% to $490.9m and adjusted EPS up 13% to $1.61, revenue above estimates; fiscal 2027 seen flat at $1.85bn revenue

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted (non-GAAP), continuing operations; GAAP diluted EPS $1.49 vs $0.43

results: Q4 revenue rose 3% to $490.9m, ahead of the $481.8m estimate: higher prices and a richer mix added 6%, while lower volumes took off 3%.
Adjusted EPS rose to $1.61 from $1.42; GAAP EPS from continuing operations was $1.49, up from $0.43 when a big tax charge hit last year.
Adjusted EBITDA grew 4% to $127.8m despite weaker volumes and higher material, labour and freight costs.
For the year, Griffon became a pure building-products company, cut debt by $364m and lowered leverage to 2.0x; free cash flow was $267m.
It bought back 1.6m shares ($136m) in fiscal 2026, added $400m to its buyback authorisation ($545m now available) and lifted the quarterly dividend 14% to $0.25.

guidance.summary: Griffon's first fiscal 2027 outlook calls for revenue and adjusted EBITDA roughly flat at $1.85bn and $460m. It expects free cash flow about equal to income from continuing operations, with $60m of capital spending and $50m of interest.

points: Management said Griffon is winning garage-door share, mainly in higher-end homes, even as the overall market shrinks with fewer new builds.
Residential volumes are expected to fall again in fiscal 2027, with a recent price increase making up the gap; commercial volume is seen flat.
The first half of fiscal 2027 is expected to trail last year slightly and the second half to come in a little ahead as pricing takes full effect.
Free cash flow will go to buybacks and paying down bank debt; small add-on acquisitions are possible. Both credit-rating agencies upgraded Griffon one notch.
Weak commercial construction (the architecture billings index is below 50) and cost inflation were the main risks named.
call.source: Griffon (GFF) Q4 2026 earnings call transcript — The Motley Fool, 17 Nov 2026

watch: Residential garage-door volumes and whether price increases hold up.
Any pick-up in housing or commercial building activity, which management says would lift growth.
Pace of buybacks under the $545m authorisation and further debt reduction.
